source_groups.Japanese: 提督、地図がないと 道に迷っちゃいますよ
source_groups.context_note: A conversational warning to the admiral sets up the map requirement.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、地図がないと 道に迷います
source_groups.context_note: Keep the measured warning and the address to the admiral. The speaker expects the party to lose its way.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、地図がないと 道に迷っちゃうよ
source_groups.context_note: The informal warning sounds more immediate than the formal version. Keep the thought tied to the absence of a map.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、地図がないと 道に迷っちまいますよ
source_groups.context_note: The speaker warns in a rougher voice that the party will get itself lost without a map.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、地図がないと 道に迷ってしまうぞ
source_groups.context_note: The firm voice treats the map as necessary for keeping their bearings.

source_groups.Japanese: ていとく、地図がないと 道に迷っちゃうよー
source_groups.context_note: The child voices a direct worry about getting lost and addresses the admiral.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、地図がないと 道に迷いますぞ
source_groups.context_note: The older, formal voice makes the same warning in a measured register.

source_groups.Japanese: 鬱蒼とした森ですね 注意して行きましょう
source_groups.context_note: The first observation describes the thick woods and suggests that the party travel carefully.

source_groups.Japanese: 鬱蒼とした森です 注意して行きましょう
source_groups.context_note: The more formal speaker notes the density of the woods and urges caution.

source_groups.Japanese: 暗いなあ ちょっと、やな感じだよ
source_groups.context_note: The speaker notices the darkness and feels uneasy. The feeling belongs to the speaker.

source_groups.Japanese: なんか鬱蒼としてるわね 道に迷わないといいけど
source_groups.context_note: The speaker comments on the thick growth and hopes the party will keep its bearings.

source_groups.Japanese: …いやな感じのする森だぜ
source_groups.context_note: The curt remark conveys unease without assigning it a cause.

source_groups.Japanese: 慎重にな。気をつけて行くぞい
source_groups.context_note: This speaker simply urges everyone to proceed carefully.

source_groups.Japanese: なんかいいもの、あるといいねー
source_groups.context_note: The eager child hopes the expedition will turn up something interesting.

source_groups.Japanese: 鬱蒼とした森ですな 何も出てこないといいですが…
source_groups.context_note: Keep the older speaker's formality and open-ended worry that something might emerge.

source_groups.Japanese: 気をつけて進もう
source_groups.context_note: Rafael suggests proceeding carefully after the crew's opening remarks.

source_groups.Japanese: て、提督、後ろ…
source_groups.context_note: The first alarm is hesitant and calls to the admiral before pointing behind the captain.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督っ、動かないでください！ 後ろに…
source_groups.context_note: The speaker urgently tells the admiral to stay still, then trails off.

source_groups.Japanese: て、提督、うしろ…
source_groups.context_note: The speaker stammers before directing the admiral's attention behind them.

source_groups.Japanese: きゃ…。う、うしろに…
source_groups.context_note: The cry comes first. A stammer delays the warning about what is behind them.

source_groups.Japanese: む！ 提督、後ろ…
source_groups.context_note: A caught breath or brief interjection leads into the warning to the admiral.

source_groups.Japanese: うわ…。う、うしろ…
source_groups.context_note: The speaker reacts with surprise and stammers through the incomplete warning.
Keep the unspoken startled reaction separate from the following spoken alarm.

source_groups.Japanese: 危ないっ！
source_groups.context_note: The brief warning cuts in after the silent reaction.

source_groups.Japanese: 勇敢に戦う
source_groups.context_note: The first option offers to stand and face the bear. The concise action wording works in the choice list.

source_groups.Japanese: 死んだふり
source_groups.context_note: Play dead is the familiar idiom and sets up the joke about Emilio.

source_groups.Japanese: その他
source_groups.context_note: The third option signals another set of choices and leaves their actions unspecified.

source_groups.Japanese: 撃って！
source_groups.context_note: Rafael gives a short order to fire at once.

source_groups.Japanese: あ！ 逃げていきました！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker reacts as the bear takes off. The exclamation belongs to that moment.

source_groups.Japanese: 熊のヤツ、逃げたよ！
source_groups.context_note: The relieved speaker says plainly that the bear has gone.

source_groups.Japanese: あ！ 逃げてったわよ！
source_groups.context_note: The surprised speaker calls out the retreat. Keep that reaction distinct from the formal variants.

source_groups.Japanese: お！ 逃げていったわい！
source_groups.context_note: Keep the older speaker's surprise at the retreat. The bear is already running off.

source_groups.Japanese: やったあ！ いっちゃったよ！
source_groups.context_note: The child celebrates after the bear leaves.

source_groups.Japanese: 水夫が少し負傷したようです
source_groups.context_note: The notice reports apparent minor injuries among the sailors. Preserve both the uncertainty and the severity.

source_groups.Japanese: て、提督… 熊のヤツ、いっこうに立ち去る気配が ありません
source_groups.context_note: The speaker stammers and reports that the bear shows no sign of leaving.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督… あの熊は、いっこうに立ち去る気配が ありません
source_groups.context_note: The formal speaker reports what the bear is doing and leaves its intentions open.

source_groups.Japanese: …ダメだ 熊のヤツ、全然動かないよ！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker is frustrated that the bear still has not moved.

source_groups.Japanese: て、提督…ダメだわ この熊、全然、動こうとしないの
source_groups.context_note: The anxious speaker hesitates and realizes that the bear still will not move.

source_groups.Japanese: て、提督…ダメだ 熊の野郎、ぜんっぜん逃げやしねえ
source_groups.context_note: The rough speaker is frustrated by the bear's persistence. Keep the contempt in the address to the animal.

source_groups.Japanese: …こりゃいかんな 熊のヤツ、いっこうに立ち去る気配が ないわい
source_groups.context_note: The older speaker recognizes the predicament because the bear shows no sign of leaving.

source_groups.Japanese: て、ていとくー… クマさん、帰る気なんてなさそう
source_groups.context_note: The child addresses the bear familiarly and imagines it going home. Preserve the tentative observation.

source_groups.Japanese: ううむ… あの熊からは動く気配が 感じられませんぞ
source_groups.context_note: The formal speaker sees no sign of movement. The scene still leaves the next action uncertain.

source_groups.Japanese: しっ、がまんして
source_groups.context_note: Rafael asks for a little longer and hushes the group.
The silent beat stays in its own panel before the next reaction.

source_groups.Japanese: ふう…、やっとあきらめたか
source_groups.context_note: The pause and then finally mark the relief after waiting.

source_groups.Japanese: ふう…、やっとあきらめたわ
source_groups.context_note: The speaker briefly exhales, then realizes the bear has finally given up.

source_groups.Japanese: ふう…、やっとあきらめやがったか
source_groups.context_note: The rough speaker exhales in relief and keeps a trace of irritation.

source_groups.Japanese: ぐう…
source_groups.context_note: The snore identifies the alternate outcome without a spoken explanation.

source_groups.Japanese: エミリオ？
source_groups.context_note: The captain's quick question marks the discovery of Emilio.

source_groups.Japanese: すう…
source_groups.context_note: The sleeping sailor's light snore answers the question directly.

source_groups.Japanese: “振り”じゃなくて 本当に寝ちゃってる…
source_groups.context_note: Rafael contrasts Emilio pretending to be asleep with actually falling asleep.

source_groups.Japanese: １日経過しました
source_groups.context_note: The system notice keeps the exact one-day passage of time.

source_groups.Japanese: 威嚇して追い払う
source_groups.context_note: This menu action means attempting to frighten the bear away. The following failure remains possible.

source_groups.Japanese: とにかく逃げる
source_groups.context_note: The second option urges immediate flight. Run for it conveys that urgency in the menu.

source_groups.Japanese: 威嚇しましたが、逃げません！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker reports an attempt to frighten the bear and its failure to run.

source_groups.Japanese: 威嚇しても逃げないとは…
source_groups.context_note: The speaker trails off after noticing that the attempt still failed.

source_groups.Japanese: なんだ、こいつ！ 脅したのに逃げやしないよ！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker reacts incredulously. The attempt to scare the bear has failed.

source_groups.Japanese: 図太いヤツね！ 脅しても逃げないわ！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker marvels at the nerve of the bear and says the attempt to frighten it failed.

source_groups.Japanese: おお？ こいつ、根性の座った熊だな 逃げやしねえ！
source_groups.context_note: The rough register makes the observation about the bear's nerve sound like grudging admiration.

source_groups.Japanese: おいおい！ 威嚇しても、ぜんぜん逃げやせん！ どうなっとるんじゃ！
source_groups.context_note: The older speaker exclaims over the failed intimidation and asks what is wrong with the bear.

source_groups.Japanese: あれえ？ 脅かしたのに逃げないよう！
source_groups.context_note: The child is puzzled because the attempt failed to make the bear run.

source_groups.Japanese: 威嚇しても逃げないとは… 図太いヤツですな
source_groups.context_note: The more formal speaker observes that the bear will not flee and remarks on its boldness.

source_groups.Japanese: まずいよ、提督！ あいつ、人食いグマかもよ！？ 下手に手を出すと こっちが危ないって！！
source_groups.context_note: The warning leaves the animal's danger uncertain and says that mishandling it could put the crew at risk.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、危ない！ くっ。…隊員が襲われました！ もう逃げないと こちらが危ないですよ！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker calls to the admiral, reports an attack on the expedition party and says they need to flee. The source gives no count.

source_groups.Japanese: ！ 危ない！ しまった…隊員が襲われました！ ここは逃げましょう！ こっちの身に危険が！
source_groups.context_note: The formal speaker reacts to the attack and urges immediate escape because the others are also in danger.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、危ないっ！ やばいな、隊員が襲われたよ！ あきらめて逃げよう！
source_groups.context_note: The alarm turns into a decision to give up the attempt and run. The attack is already reported and the source gives no count.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、危ないっ！ ちょっと、隊員が襲われてるわ！ もう逃げたほうがいいわよっ！
source_groups.context_note: The attack is still happening. The speaker tells the admiral to leave.

source_groups.Japanese: 危ねえっ！！ くそっ、何人かケガしちまったか！？ ここは、逃げたほうがいいぜ！
source_groups.context_note: Keep the rough interjection and the question about whether some of the group were injured.

source_groups.Japanese: 危ないぞ！ 提督、ここは逃げたほうがええ！！
source_groups.context_note: The urgent address to the admiral calls for escape. Keep the older voice without stiff prose.

source_groups.Japanese: あぶないよう！ 逃げようよう！！
source_groups.context_note: The child's fear becomes an urgent request to run.

source_groups.Japanese: こりゃ、まずい 提督、逃げたほうがいい！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker recognizes the danger and tells the admiral that flight is the better course.

source_groups.Japanese: 水夫の疲労がだいぶ上がりました 負傷者がでたようです
source_groups.context_note: The system message reports a considerable rise in fatigue and apparent injuries. Keep the separate outcomes.

source_groups.Japanese: 逃げよう！！
source_groups.context_note: Rafael gives the immediate command to run.

source_groups.Japanese: 何とか逃げることができました…
source_groups.context_note: The relieved speaker says they somehow got away and pauses to catch their breath.

source_groups.Japanese: ふう … 逃げることができました…
source_groups.context_note: The formal variant makes a separate pause before reporting the escape.

source_groups.Japanese: はあはあ… 助かったみたいだね…
source_groups.context_note: Panting comes first, then the tentative realization that the party is safe.

source_groups.Japanese: …助かったみたいね…
source_groups.context_note: The speaker makes a tentative assessment after getting away.

source_groups.Japanese: ふう… 逃げ切れたか…
source_groups.context_note: The brief relief still leaves the speaker asking whether they lost the bear.

source_groups.Japanese: ふうふう… ああ、こわかったよう…
source_groups.context_note: The child pants and says how frightened they were.

source_groups.Japanese: おお、息が切れる… みんな、助かったようですな よかった
source_groups.context_note: The formal older speaker runs out of breath, takes stock of the others and expresses relief.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、森を抜けました！ 遺跡に到着しました
source_groups.context_note: The speaker announces two milestones to the admiral. The party is out of the forest and at the ruins.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、森を抜けました ここが遺跡か…
source_groups.context_note: The speaker addresses the admiral and takes in the sight of the ruins after crossing the forest.

source_groups.Japanese: ようやく森を抜け出したね… あっ…！ 提督、ここが遺跡なんだね！
source_groups.context_note: The relief of getting through the woods is followed by a sudden, confident recognition of the ruins.

source_groups.Japanese: ようやく森を抜けましたね ここが…遺跡なのね
source_groups.context_note: The speaker says they are finally out and pauses before recognizing the ruins.

source_groups.Japanese: おおっ！ 提督！ 森を抜けたぜ！！ うん。あれが遺跡だな！
source_groups.context_note: The rough speaker greets the admiral with relief before recognizing the ruins.

source_groups.Japanese: おお。森を抜けることができたぞい … うむ。あれが遺跡かの
source_groups.context_note: The older speaker celebrates getting through the forest and asks whether those are the ruins.

source_groups.Japanese: わーい。森から出られたよ！ んーと。変な石がいっぱいあるけど… …遺跡って、あれのことかな？
source_groups.context_note: The child celebrates getting out, notices the odd stones and wonders if they are the ruins.

source_groups.Japanese: 提督、森を抜けましたな おお…ここが遺跡か…
source_groups.context_note: The older speaker announces the crossing to the admiral, then pauses to recognize the ruins.

source_groups.Japanese: あれかな？ 変な人たちの集まりっていうのは？
source_groups.context_note: Rafael asks about the group they heard about before the chant begins.

source_groups.Japanese: あああ～～～…
source_groups.context_note: The drawn-out voice establishes the start of the chant.

source_groups.Japanese: おおお～～～！
source_groups.context_note: The next voice keeps its separate prolonged cry.

source_groups.Japanese: う、歌？ なんか危ねえ雰囲気だぞ
source_groups.context_note: The stammer and unease work as the listeners recognize that the voices might be singing.

source_groups.Japanese: 日は巡り、月は巡り、星は巡る 光と闇が拮抗するとき 其れもまた光と闇の狭間に在り
source_groups.context_note: The repeated motion of the sun, moon and stars and the balance of light and darkness are intentional ritual imagery.
The single puzzled reaction falls between the chant and the crew's own question.

source_groups.Japanese: ヤツら、何言ってやがんだ？ まじないか？
source_groups.context_note: The rough question guesses that the words may be a spell without identifying what they are.

source_groups.Japanese: 我々『古代巨石文明研究会』が 神託を手にするときは近づいている！ そして、いよいよ世界制圧の野望を 実現するのだ！
source_groups.context_note: Keep the society's established name, expectation of a revelation and ambition to rule the world.

source_groups.Japanese: お告げの日の前夜より、再び祈りを 捧げる！ 我々を侮辱した、愚かなる輩を 生け贄に捧げるのだ！
source_groups.context_note: The speaker orders prayers to start again on the eve of the revelation and threatens a sacrifice.

source_groups.Japanese: おおう！
source_groups.context_note: The congregation's response stays brief and separate from the crew's reactions.

source_groups.Japanese: 世界制圧！？
source_groups.context_note: The shocked question repeats the society's goal.

source_groups.Japanese: 生け贄だあ？ マジかよ、こいつら！？
source_groups.context_note: The other response reacts to the threatened sacrifice and the group's seriousness.

source_groups.Japanese: それまでは巨石に近づかぬように！ 本日は、これにて解散する！
source_groups.context_note: The society leader gives a final order about the stones and formally ends the meeting.

source_groups.Japanese: 行っちゃった
source_groups.context_note: Rafael notes the group's departure before the crew suggests investigating.

source_groups.Japanese: 行ってみようぜ
source_groups.context_note: The suggestion to look follows the departure and keeps the conversation moving.

source_groups.Japanese: …行くぞ
source_groups.context_note: Hodram's short decision to move retains his restraint and the beat before action.

source_groups.Japanese: 撃て！
source_groups.context_note: The order to fire is immediate and plain.

source_groups.Japanese: しっ、がまんしろ
source_groups.context_note: Hodram asks for quiet and patience while they wait out the bear.

source_groups.Japanese: 本当に寝てやがる…
source_groups.context_note: Hodram realizes that the sailor really fell asleep.

source_groups.Japanese: 走れ！！
source_groups.context_note: The command to run is abrupt and urgent.

source_groups.Japanese: さあ、行くわよ！
source_groups.context_note: Lil leads the group onward directly.

source_groups.Japanese: 撃つのよっ！
source_groups.context_note: Lil's immediate command refers to the bear in front of them.

source_groups.Japanese: しっ、がまんするの！
source_groups.context_note: Lil hushes the party and asks them to hold still in the waiting branch.

source_groups.Japanese: あれっ？ エミリオは？
source_groups.context_note: Lil's surprise at Emilio's absence leads directly into the sleeping reveal.

source_groups.Japanese: 死んだフリって言ったのに ホントに寝てる…。あきれた
source_groups.context_note: Lil contrasts the order to play dead with actually falling asleep and ends with disbelief.

source_groups.Japanese: 逃げるわよ！！
source_groups.context_note: The captain calls for flight when the situation turns dangerous.

source_groups.Japanese: 行きましょうか
source_groups.context_note: Maria's measured question invites the party to continue.

source_groups.Japanese: …もう少しの辛抱よ
source_groups.context_note: Maria asks the party to endure the wait for a little longer.

source_groups.Japanese: 寝てるわ…
source_groups.context_note: Maria recognizes that Emilio is asleep after the snore.
